AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Ultrasound-guided lumbar plexus blocks usually require confirmatory neurostimulation. A simpler alternative is to inject local anaesthetic inside the posteromedial quadrant of the psoas muscle under ultrasound guidance.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: We hypothesised that both techniques would result in similar total anaesthesia time, defined as the sum of performance and onset time.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: A randomised, observer-blinded, equivalence trial (equivalence margin = 7.4 min).

AbstractText.Label: SETTING
AbstractText.content: Ramathibodi Hospital and Maharaj Nakorn Chiang Mai Hospital (Thailand) from 12 May 2016 to 10 January 2017.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENTS
AbstractText.content: A total of 110 patients undergoing total hip or knee arthroplasty, who required lumbar plexus block for postoperative analgesia.

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTION
AbstractText.content: In the combined ultrasonography-neurostimulation group, quadriceps-evoked motor response was sought at a current between 0.2 and 0.8 mA prior to local anaesthetic injection (30 ml of lidocaine 1% and levobupivacaine 0.25% with epinephrine 5 μg ml and 5 mg of dexamethasone). In the ultrasound guidance alone group, local anaesthetic was simply injected inside the posteromedial quadrant of the psoas muscle.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN OUTCOMES MEASURES
AbstractText.content: We measured the total anaesthesia time, the success rate (at 30 min), the number of needle passes, block-related pain, cumulative opioid consumption (at 24 h) and adverse events (vascular puncture, paraesthesia, local anaesthetic spread to the epidural space).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Compared with ultrasound guidance alone, combined ultrasonography-neurostimulation resulted in decreased mean (±SD) total anaesthesia time [15.3 (±6.5) vs. 20.1 (±9.0) min; mean difference, -4.8; 95% confidence interval, -8.1 to -1.9; P = 0.005] and mean (±SD) onset time [10.2 (±5.6) vs. 15.5 (±9.0) min; P = 0.004). No inter-group differences were observed in terms of success rate, performance time, number of needle passes, block-related pain, opioid consumption or adverse events.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Although the ultrasonography-neurostimulation technique results in a shorter total anaesthesia time compared with ultrasound guidance alone, this difference falls within our accepted equivalence margin (±7.4 min).

Article.ArticleTitle: Ultrasound with neurostimulation compared with ultrasound guidance alone for lumbar plexus block: A randomised single blinded equivalence trial.
